primaryReferences.contentUsedParaphrase: The epidermis contains paired guard cells around gas-exchange openings. Guard cells commonly occur most densely on leaf undersides, though they may also occur on upper surfaces and stems. Ordinary epidermal cells normally have few or no chloroplasts.
The leaf epidermis has stomatal pores bordered by a pair of guard cells. Chloroplasts occur in guard cells; the epidermal background is distinct from the photosynthetic mesophyll.

reasoning: The edited artwork is a typical simplified broadleaf underside example consistent with both primary textbook descriptions. No universal underside-only rule or mesophyll-as-epidermis interpretation is used.
